scope: Repository tree scan using GitHub recursive Git Trees API; file counts below reflect scanned default-branch trees. This is a migration backlog, not a claim that ports are complete.
acceptance_gates: Identify source behavior and dependencies before porting.
Create Python 3.11+ module without deleting or replacing the original.
Add unit tests and deterministic fixtures for behavior and failure cases.
Add Tkinter GUI or browser-compatible frontend as appropriate.
Run tests on Linux and Windows CI; package with PyInstaller where a desktop executable is useful.
Publish version, platform requirements, SHA-256 checksums and build evidence.
Promote only after parity and platform acceptance; native kernel, boot, driver and assembly code remains native.

repositories.next: Add parity tests and Python API/GUI wrappers for browser tools; keep static frontends static.
Inventory requirements and tests per module; standardize launch commands and build independent GUI executables.
Reuse existing Python implementations; package standalone GUI/CLI tools after tests.
Port independent asset and network management utilities, with safe scope and offline tests.
Package reusable Python components and compare game/asset behaviors against existing vectors.
Port host-side ISO/build/diagnostic tools first; do not replace Koronos, drivers, bootloader or assembly.
Avoid duplicating vendor changes; sync verified upstream Python tools and add Octavian-specific tests.
Convert prototypes into tested reusable modules and GUI wrappers.
Port simulator core against instruction/register/flag vectors before UI rewrite.
Define cryptographic test vectors and secret-handling rules before porting key-generation behavior.
Implement instruction-level Python reference simulator only where reference semantics are documented.
Audit existing Python document/Thamudic tools and build GUI packaging around tested functions.
Use published test vectors; never log private keys, seed phrases or credentials.
Prioritize defensive audit utilities; add rate limits and safe local-only tests; do not expose credential attacks.
Share portable business logic in Python where it helps; preserve platform-native app shell.

prioritization: P0 means immediate tools/portfolio; P1 means existing Python and host-side utilities; P2 means mixed-language apps requiring behavioral tests; P3 means platform-native prototypes.
